title: Type Juggling and Type Conversion
learning_outcomes: Explain what type juggling and type conversion contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: automatic type conversion.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Reliable programs represent values deliberately. Variables hold changing values, constants name stable values, and type behavior affects comparisons, conversion, function contracts, and error handling. In this lesson, focus on automatic type conversion; then compare it with explicit casting. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use type juggling and type conversion when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Reliable programs represent values deliberately. Variables hold changing values, constants name stable values, and type behavior affects comparisons, conversion, function contracts, and error handling. For type juggling and type conversion, begin with automatic type conversion. Also distinguish explicit casting; numeric strings; boolean conversion. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
